title: Multimodal Perception Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Methods that combine vision, audio, text, and sensor readings into unified perception. The Multimodal Perception Database documents perception that uses more than one sense: combining camera, lidar, audio, text, and proprioception into a single understanding of the scene. One sensor lies or goes blind — cameras fail in darkness, lidar in rain, microphones in noise — so fusion is about graceful degradation: the record shows how each modality contributes, what happens when one drops, and the measured gain of the combination over any single sense.

title: Multimodal Perception Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Fusion levels: early (concatenate raw/sensor features — needs tight calibration), late (combine decisions — robust, simple), intermediate/cross-attention (queries from one modality attend to another — the modern default), mixture-of-experts per modality with gating. Calibration: spatial (extrinsics: rotation/translation between sensors, from checkerboards or motion), temporal (timestamp alignment, interpolation to a common clock). Synchronization: hardware trigger preferred; software sync bounds the error. Degradation design: train/evaluate with modality dropout so the system learns to cope; report the full dropout table. Metrics: per-modality ablation gain = fusion score - best single score; robustness = worst-case dropout score. Failure modes: miscalibration (silent killer — monitor reprojection/feature alignment online), clock drift, one modality dominating training.

demo.title: Execution: A* pathfinding on a grid
demo.code: const grid=[[0,0,0,1],[0,1,0,0],[0,0,0,0]];const W=4,H=3;function h(a,b){return Math.abs(a[0]-b[0])+Math.abs(a[1]-b[1]);}function astar(s,g){const open=[{p:s,f:h(s,g),c:0}],came={},cost={[s]:0};while(open.length){open.sort((a,b)=>a.f-b.f);const cur=open.shift();if(cur.p[0]===g[0]&&cur.p[1]===g[1]){const path=[g];let k=g+'';while(came[k]){path.unshift(came[k]);k=came[k]+'';}return path;}for(const [dx,dy] of [[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]]){const n=[cur.p[0]+dx,cur.p[1]+dy];if(n[0]<0||n[1]<0||n[0]>=H||n[1]>=W||grid[n[0]][n[1]])continue;const nc=cur.c+1;if(cost[n+'']===undefined||nc<cost[n+'']){cost[n+'']=nc;came[n+'']=cur.p;open.push({p:n,f:nc+h(n,g),c:nc});}}}}const path=astar([0,0],[2,3]);J({steps:path.length-1});assert(path.length-1===5,'astar');

title: Multimodal Perception Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: gain test (fusion >= best single modality on test data); dropout test (tables complete for all subsets); calibration test (errors within tolerance); determinism test. Limitations: demos use score tables; real fusion needs synchronized datasets; gating behavior needs degraded-condition data. Every design includes its dropout table.

demo.title: Execution: Hohmann transfer delta-v
demo.code: const mu=398600;function circ(r){return Math.sqrt(mu/r);}const r1=6678,r2=42164;const a=(r1+r2)/2;const dv1=Math.abs(Math.sqrt(mu*(2/r1-1/a))-circ(r1));const dv2=Math.abs(circ(r2)-Math.sqrt(mu*(2/r2-1/a)));J({dv1:+dv1.toFixed(2),dv2:+dv2.toFixed(2),total:+(dv1+dv2).toFixed(2)});assert(dv1+dv2>3.8&&dv1+dv2<4.0,'hohmann');
